info.title: SE Ranking Data API
info.description:
The Data API returns SEO data for any domain, URL or keyword: backlink profiles, domain traffic and keyword rankings, keyword research, AI search visibility, SERP results and website audits. Requests are billed in API credits.

## Authentication

All endpoints are served from `https://api.seranking.com` and use one SE Ranking API key, the same key for the Data API, the Project API, the Local Marketing API and the SE Visible API. Send it in the `Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY` header (recommended) or as the `apikey` query parameter. See [Getting API access](https://seranking.com/api/how-to-get-api/).

Rate limits: [API rate limits](https://seranking.com/api/rate-limits/). Credits: [API credit system](https://seranking.com/api/api-credits-system/).

tags.name: Backlinks
tags.description:
**[Backlinks API](https://seranking.com/backlinks-api.html)** retrieves backlink data for a target domain, host, or URL. It provides aggregated metrics such as counts of backlinks, referring domains, IPs, and subnets, as well as anchor texts, top pages, TLDs, and countries. The API includes endpoints for summary metrics, historical data, raw backlink lists, export options, and authority scores. Data is refreshed on a monthly basis.

Using the API, you can:

- retrieve backlink summary metrics, including counts of backlinks, referring domains, IPs, subnets, top anchors, TLDs, and countries

- retrieve key backlink metrics in batch for multiple targets

- list all backlinks for a single target

- fetch backlinks in batches for large datasets

- track new, lost, cumulative, and daily backlink changes

- retrieve backlink anchor texts

- access referring domains, including counts and new/lost domains

- access referring IPs and subnets, including counts

- list indexed pages with backlinks

- retrieve page and domain authority metrics, including distributions, histograms, and historical values

- export backlink data for large-scale analysis

Documentation: [Backlinks](https://seranking.com/api/data/backlinks/)

tags.name: Domain Analysis
tags.description:
**Domain Analysis API** provides detailed insights into a domain’s search performance. Data is refreshed on a monthly basis.

Using the API, you can:

- query regional or worldwide data

- retrieve keyword statistics, domain pages, and subdomains

- analyze competitors to identify common keywords and keyword gaps

- retrieve paid advertising data, including ad creatives, observed positions, and traffic

- access historical data to track changes in rankings, traffic, and ad performance

- filter and sort results by metrics such as search volume, CPC, competition, keyword difficulty, and ranking positions

Documentation: [Domain Analysis](https://seranking.com/api/data/domain-analysis/)

tags.name: Keyword Research
tags.description:
**[Keyword Research API](https://seranking.com/keyword-research-api.html)** provides programmatic access to keyword metrics and discovery. Data is refreshed on a monthly basis.

Using the API, you can:

- retrieve keyword metrics such as search volume, CPC, competition, difficulty, and historical trends

- discover similar keywords with the same user intent

- find related keywords based on overlapping search results

- get question keywords associated with a seed keyword

- discover long-tail keywords that are lower-volume and more specific

Documentation: [Keyword Research](https://seranking.com/api/data/keyword-research/)

tags.name: AI Search
tags.description:
**AI Search API** provides programmatic access to a domain’s performance in Large Language Model (LLM) results. Data is refreshed on a monthly basis.

Using the API, you can:

- get an AI search overview with metrics like link presence, average position, AI traffic, and historical trends

- compare a primary domain against competitors across multiple LLM engines and retrieve a share of voice leaderboard

- discover the brand associated with a domain or URL

- retrieve prompts by target, showing where a domain or URL appears in LLM responses

- retrieve prompts by brand, showing where a brand is mentioned in LLM results

Documentation: [AI Search](https://seranking.com/api/data/ai-search/)

tags.name: SERP
tags.description:
The following limits apply to the SERP API:

- Up to **1500 SERP tasks** can run in parallel.

- Up to **10 keywords per task** can be submitted by default.

- Up to **10 tasks per second** can be created.

Contact [api@seranking.com](mailto:api@seranking.com) to discuss your volume needs and custom limits.

**SERP API** provides programmatic access to Google search engine results pages (SERPs) for specified keywords. Results are retrieved on demand.

Using the API, you can:

- Submit SERP collection tasks for one or more keywords across specific locations, languages, and devices

- Retrieve standard SERP results, including organic results, ads, and featured snippets

- Retrieve advanced SERP results with full SERP items and features

- Download raw HTML dumps of Google search results pages

- List recent SERP tasks created within the last 24 hours

- Retrieve available search locations

Documentation: [SERP](https://seranking.com/api/data/serp/)

tags.name: Website Audit
tags.description:
**[Website Audit API](https://seranking.com/website-audit-api.html)** provides programmatic access to technical SEO audits. Results are retrieved on demand.

Using the API, you can:

- Create website audits using standard HTML crawling or JavaScript-rendered crawling

- Track audit execution by checking audit status, progress, and crawl statistics in real time

- Retrieve audit results, including health scores and categorized issues

- Analyze pages and audit issues, including page-level technical metrics and URLs affected by specific issues

- Analyze link data, including internal and external links discovered during the crawl

- Manage audits by listing, filtering, renaming, deleting, and accessing historical audit snapshots

Documentation: [Website Audit](https://seranking.com/api/data/website-audit/)

tags.name: Account System
tags.description:
**Account System API** provides programmatic access to your SE Ranking Data API subscription and usage information.

Using the API, you can:

- Get subscription details, including plan status, start, and expiration dates

- Check your remaining API balance (units left)

- Monitor usage programmatically to manage quotas

Documentation: [Account System](https://seranking.com/api/data/account-system/)

**Cost:** 1 credit per backlink

- The `apikey` (required) and `output` (optional) parameters must always be included as GET parameters, even if other parameters are sent via POST.

- Any POST data in the request body should be in JSON format.

parameters.name: target

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description:

• `domain` – analyzes all URLs in the domain, including subdomains.
• `host` – analyzes all URLs under this host only (subdomains excluded).
• `url` – analyzes a single, specific URL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return. Must be within the range: `[1, 10,000]`.

parameters.name: per_domain
parameters.description:
Number of backlinks to return per referring domain. Must be within the range: `[1, 100]`. For example, when set to `1`, each returned backlink comes from a different referring domain.

If empty, all backlinks are returned.

parameters.name: output
parameters.description: Response format (`json` or `xml`). Must always be sent as a GET parameter.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description:
Field by which results are sorted:
• `date_found` – returns the most recent backlinks first.
• `domain_inlink_rank` – returns backlinks with the highest Domain InLink Rank first.
• `inlink_rank` – returns backlinks with the highest InLink Rank first.

parameters.name: inlink_rank_from
parameters.description: Minimum InLink Rank. Returns backlinks ≥ this value. Must be within the range: `[0, 100]`.

parameters.name: inlink_rank_to
parameters.description: Maximum InLink Rank. Returns backlinks ≤ this value. Must be within the range: `[0, 100]`.

parameters.description: Minimum Domain InLink Rank. Returns backlinks ≥ this value. Must be within the range: `[0, 100]`.

parameters.name: domain_inlink_rank_to
parameters.description: Maximum Domain InLink Rank. Returns backlinks ≤ this value. Must be within the range: `[0, 100]`.

parameters.description: Text filter for referring page URL (e.g., `seo-software`). Maximum 2063 ASCII symbols.

parameters.name: url_from_filter_mode
parameters.description:
Filter mode:
• `contains` – returns backlinks where `url_from` contains `url_from_filter` text.
• `does_not_contain` – returns backlinks where `url_from` doesn’t contain `url_from_filter` text.

Ignored if `url_from_filter` parameter is not set.

parameters.name: url_to_filter
parameters.description: Text filter for destination URL (e.g., `seranking.com/blog/`). Maximum 2063 ASCII symbols.

• `contains` – returns backlinks where `url_to` contains `url_to_filter` text.
• `does_not_contain` – returns backlinks where `url_to` doesn’t contain `url_to_filter` text.

Ignored if `url_to_filter` parameter is not set.

parameters.description: Text filter for link anchor (e.g., `seo`). Maximum 2063 ASCII symbols.

parameters.description:
Filter mode:
• `contains` – returns backlinks where `anchor` contains `anchor_filter` text.
• `does_not_contain` – returns backlinks where `anchor` doesn’t contain `anchor_filter` text.

Ignored if `anchor_filter` parameter is not set.

parameters.name: nofollow_filter
parameters.description:
Filter mode:
• `nofollow_only` – returns only backlinks classified as nofollow.
• `dofollow_only` – returns only backlinks classified as dofollow.

If empty, all backlinks are returned.

get.description:
Returns all backlinks pointing to a target using cursor-based pagination. Backlinks are delivered in sequential batches. This method supports pagination and doesn’t provide sorting or filtering. Unlike the [List all backlinks](https://seranking.com/api/data/backlinks#all) method, which supports ordering (e.g., by InLink Rank or recency), this endpoint is designed for complete backlink retrieval, batch by batch.

Pagination is handled via a cursor (`next` parameter). The cursor marks a specific position in the dataset and remains valid unless the item is removed. Cursors are typically valid for up to 24 hours, even if new backlinks are added.

- The `next` parameter must **not** be included when requesting the first page of data. Doing so will return an error.

- If the response doesn’t return `next`, you have reached the last page of data.

**Cost:** 1 credit per backlink

• `host` – analyzes all URLs under this host only (subdomains excluded).
• `url` – analyzes a single, specific URL.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Maximum number of results to return in one page. Must be within the range: `[1, 100,000]`.

Default: 10,000

parameters.name: next
parameters.description:
Cursor pointing to the end of the previously returned page. 
• Must not be included for the first page request.
• Not returned in the last page of data.

parameters.name: per_domain
parameters.description:
Number of sample backlinks to return per referring domain instead of all backlinks. Must be within the range: `[1, 100]`. For example, when set to `1`, each returned backlink comes from a different referring domain.

If empty, all backlinks are returned.

get.description:
Returns the keywords a domain (or a specific URL) ranks for in a regional database, organic or paid. Supports historical month-by-month snapshots, advanced filtering across keyword properties, SERP-feature presence, search intent, and traffic share.

**Cost:** 100 credits per request

Either `domain` or `url` must be supplied. **If both are sent, `url` takes precedence and `domain` is silently dropped.**

**Historical snapshots (year / month)**

- Both omitted → current snapshot.

- Both supplied with a month within the retention window → historical snapshot.

- Only one of the two supplied → current snapshot (the lone parameter is silently ignored — there is no error).

- Future date → current snapshot (silent fallback).

- Date older than the retention window → empty array `[]`.

⚠ **Historical responses use a different schema than current responses.** See [Response shape — historical](#response-shape-historical-year-month) below. Clients that consume both must branch on whether `year`/`month` were sent.

**Filters**

All filter keys use bracket-path syntax (`filter[name]=value` or `filter[name][from]=value`). Filters within a single key combine with AND; multiple values within one filter combine with OR.

**Range filters (from / to)**

All accept any combination of `from` and `to`; either bound can be omitted.

**Text filters**

JSON-encoded value; see [Text search JSON structure](#).

**Current**

If the request succeeds, the server returns an HTTP 200 with a JSON array of keyword objects. The default response includes 16 fields; request `cols=` to project a subset.

**Default response columns**

For `type=adv` (paid search), the `block` and `snippet_*` family are also returned when explicitly requested.

**Field reference**

📝 `kei` (Keyword Effectiveness Index) is accepted as an `order_field` value but is **not** a selectable response column. Requesting `cols=kei` silently drops it.

**Historical (year + month)**

When a request includes valid `year` and `month`, the upstream returns data from a different store with a different schema. Five fields are renamed or retyped, and two are dropped:

Clients consuming both shapes should branch on whether `year`/`month` were sent.

get.description:
Analyzes and compares the keyword rankings of two websites using either domains or full URLs. It can find keywords they have in common or identify a ‘keyword gap’— keywords for which one site ranks, but the other does not. This is useful for competitive analysis and identifying ranking opportunities.

**Cost:** 100 credits per request

**Note:** Either `domain` or `url` must be specified.
When one option is provided, the other is ignored.

**Understanding the diff parameter**

The `diff` parameter controls the comparison mode by defining which set of keywords to return. For these examples, let **A** be the primary `domain` and **B** be the `compare` domain.

**diff=0: common keywords (A ∩ B)**

Returns keywords for which **both** the primary `domain` (A) and the `compare` domain (B) rank.

**diff=1: keyword gap (A – B)**

Returns keywords for which the primary `domain` (A) ranks, but the `compare` domain (B) does **not**.

To find the keywords for which the compare domain ranks but your primary domain does not, simply swap the domains in your request. Set the competitor’s domain as the primary domain and your domain as the compare domain, while keeping `diff=1`.

For example, to see keywords `hotels.com` has that `booking.com` lacks, request: `...&domain=hotels.com&compare=booking.com&diff=1...`

If the request is successful, the server returns a JSON array. Each object in this array represents a keyword and includes metrics for both the primary domain and the compare domain (where applicable, depending on the diff mode).

post.description:
Retrieves various data points for a list of specified keywords within a given regional database. It’s designed for bulk analysis and returns metrics like search volume, CPC, competition, keyword difficulty, search intent, and historical search volume trends for each submitted keyword.

By default, the returned `history_trend` covers the **12 most recent months, ending at the current month**. Use the optional `history_to` parameter to end the window at an earlier month, and `history_from` to start it later — together they return a custom date range (e.g. to reconstruct a keyword’s seasonality as of a past date). The window is always **capped at 12 months**.

**Cost:** 100 credits per request

If successful, the server returns a JSON array. Each object in this array corresponds to one of the keywords submitted in the request and contains the requested data points.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Country code of the regional keyword database (e.g., `us`). For acceptable values, see Regional database codes.

keywords.description: Array of keywords to analyze, e.g. `["seo platform", "seranking.com"]`. Between 1 and 5,000 keywords per request.

sort.description: Field the results are sorted by: `volume`, `cpc`, `difficulty`, or `competition`.

history_from.description: Start month of the `history_trend` window, `YYYY-MM-DD` (the day is ignored). **Only takes effect together with `history_to`** — sent on its own it is ignored. The window then runs from `history_from` through `history_to` inclusive, capped at the most recent 12 months. Must not be later than `history_to`.

history_to.description: End month of the `history_trend` window, `YYYY-MM-DD` (the day is ignored). On its own it returns the **12 months ending at this month** — e.g. `2024-05-01` returns `2023-06-01` through `2024-05-01`. Combine with `history_from` for a shorter range. Must not be a future month.

is_data_found.description: Indicates whether data was successfully found and retrieved for this specific keyword: `true` (found) / `false` (otherwise).

keyword.description: Keyword phrase as submitted in the request.

volume.description: Average monthly search volume for this keyword in the specified source database.

cpc.description: Average Cost Per Click for this keyword.

competition.description: Paid-search competition level for this keyword, on a 0–1 scale (higher = more competition).

difficulty.description: Keyword difficulty — how hard it is to rank organically for this keyword, on a 0–100 scale (higher = harder).

items.description: Array of search intent codes. Possible values: `I` (Informational — user is looking for information), `C` (Commercial — user is investigating products, services, or brands), `T` (Transactional — user wants to complete an action or purchase), `L` (Local — user is looking for a location or something nearby), `N` (Navigational — user is looking for a specific website or page).

intents.description: Array of search intent codes. Possible values: `I` (Informational — user is looking for information), `C` (Commercial — user is investigating products, services, or brands), `T` (Transactional — user wants to complete an action or purchase), `L` (Local — user is looking for a location or something nearby), `N` (Navigational — user is looking for a specific website or page).

history_trend.description: Object containing historical search volume data for the keyword. Each key is a `YYYY-MM-DD` string representing the first day of a month, and the value is the search volume for that month. By default the window covers the 12 months ending at the current month; it is shifted by `history_to` and narrowed by `history_from` (see Request).

post.description:
Adds one or more search queries to the queue for SERP collection. Each task returns SERP results for the specified keywords, retrievable via the [Get standard SERP results](https://seranking.com/api/data/serp#standard-results) or [Get advanced SERP results](https://seranking.com/api/data/serp#advanced-results) endpoints.

When tasks are complete, the system automatically sends webhook notifications if the `pingback_url` parameter is set. This allows you to avoid repeatedly checking for task status (for more information, see [Pingback notifications](https://seranking.com/api/data/serp/#pingback-notifications)).

**Note:** The method supports **Google** search results only. **Bing** and **Yahoo!** are in development — contact [api@seranking.com](mailto:api@seranking.com) for release updates.

**Warning:** Up to **1500 SERP tasks** can run in parallel. Requests exceeding this limit return a `429 Too Many Requests` response with a `processing_limit_exceeded` error, for example:

```
{
    "error": {
        "code": "processing_limit_exceeded",
        "details": {
            "limit": 1500,
            "current_active_count": 1503,
            "requested_count": 10
        }
    },
    "message": "Processing limit exceeded. You have 1503 active tasks, which exceeds the limit of 1500. Please wait for the pending tasks to complete."
}
  
```

**Cost:** 10 credits per keyword

**Note:** One of `location_id` or `google_ads_location_id` must be provided.

**Pingback notifications**

When `pingback_url` is provided in the request, the system sends an HTTP GET request to the specified URL once the asynchronous task finishes.

- Include `$id` and `$tag` as they are in your URL.

- Upon task completion, the system substitutes these with actual values and calls the URL.

**Note:** The `$tag` value is URL-encoded if it contains special characters.

- Request: `"pingback_url": "https://your-server.com/callback?id=$id&tag=$tag"`.

- Task completes with, e.g., ID `385103` and tag `campaign_abc`.

- System calls: `GET https://your-server.com/callback?id=385103&tag=campaign_abc`.

- Requests timeout after 5 seconds.

- Failed deliveries retry up to 3 times (at ~1 min, ~5 min, ~15 min intervals).

- Success requires an `HTTP` `2xx` response from your server.

- Requests use User-Agent: `SE-Ranking-Pingback/1.0`.

- Private and internal IPs are blocked (for SSRF protection).

**Expected SERP**

Use `expected_serp` to pass what you already know about the SERP of a keyword, for example the domains you saw in its top 10 last time. It is a reference for checking the collected SERP. It does not filter or reorder the returned results, and it does not change the cost.

- Every field is optional: the parameter itself, any item and any field of an item.

- Domains are host names such as `example.com`, not URLs. They are validated by syntax only, without a DNS lookup. URLs, IP addresses and names without a top-level domain are rejected.

- Domains are converted to lower case and punycode. `www.` and duplicate domains are removed.

- `position` can only be set together with `domain`.

**Errors:** if any value is invalid, the request returns `400 Bad Request` and no tasks are created. The message names the field, for example:

```
{
  "message": "Invalid expected_serp[1].top10_domains[1]. Must be a valid domain."
}
```

If successful, the server returns an array of task objects, each representing a submitted query.

get.description:
Retrieves the full, detailed report for a completed website audit. The report includes the site’s overall health score, domain properties, and a section-by-section breakdown of all checks performed, categorized by issue type (errors, warnings, notices).

**Cost:** 0 credits

If successful, the server returns a JSON object containing the complete audit report.

- `code`: A unique identifier for the check (e.g., no_https).

- `status`: The result of the check (error, warning, notice, passed).

- `name`: A human-readable name for the check.

- `value`: The number of pages affected by this issue.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of every hyperlink (e.g., in `<a>` tags, canonicals) discovered across the entire site during the audit. It allows for a complete analysis of all internal and outbound links.

**Cost:** 0 credits

**Advanced filtering**

To build complex queries, you can add an array of `filter` parameters to the URL query string. This allows you to chain multiple conditions together using logical operators.

- `filter[index][param]`: **(Required)** The field you want to filter on.

- `filter[index][value]`: **(Required)** The value to match.

- `filter[index][type]`: The logical operator (`and` or `or`) to connect this condition to the previous one. This is **required for the second condition onwards** (i.e., for `filter[1]`, `filter[2]`, etc.).

**Example 1: OR logic**

To find all internal links that have a status code of either `301` **OR** `302`.

- `filter[0]` sets the base condition (`status = 301`).

- `filter[1][type]=or` **explicitly connects** the next condition (`status = 302`) with an **OR**.

**Example 2: AND logic**

To find all broken (`404`) image links (`anchor_type = image`).

- `filter[0]` sets the base condition (`status = 404`).

- `filter[1][type]=and` **must be included** to connect the second condition (`anchor_type = image`) with an **AND**. Omitting it would result in an error.

If successful, the server returns a JSON object containing the total count of links and an array of link objects.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the audit.

Default: all
